name: Dubrovnik
title: Dubrovnik Ship Gauging: UTM for Cruise Ships and Ferries
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging in Dubrovnik (Gruž) for cruise ships, island and Bari ferries and coasters: scrubber piping, hull and deck structure.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement at the Port of Gruž, Dubrovnik
intro: Dubrovnik's commercial harbour is at Gruž, a sheltered inlet north of the old town where cruise ships, island ferries, the Bari ro-pax service and a modest flow of coastal cargo share a handful of quays. Gauging here is driven by cruise scrubber systems, ferry refit planning and sales of small tonnage in the southern Adriatic. Atlantis NDT keeps no staff in Croatia: ultrasonic thickness technicians fly in from India once the superintendent has fixed the scope and the ship's schedule.

highlights.p: Many large cruise ships that call at Dubrovnik run exhaust gas cleaning systems, so wash-water and overboard piping near the shell is a recurring gauging scope, fitted into a call day around passenger and tender operations.

highlights.h: Island ferries and the Bari crossing
highlights.p: Car ferries to the Elafiti islands and Mljet, and the ro-pax service to Bari, work out of Gruž all year. Vehicle decks, ramps and ballast tanks can be gauged in blocks across turnarounds or in winter lay-up.
The inlet behind the Franjo Tuđman Bridge is calm in most weather, which suits owner's condition gauging and pre-purchase work on small ships and yachts alongside or on a lay-by berth.

port.h: The port of Gruž and the approach to Dubrovnik
p: Ships bound for Dubrovnik do not berth at the old town. They come up the coast, pass the island of Lokrum and the Elafiti group, and enter the long inlet of Rijeka Dubrovačka, where Gruž lies on the northern shore beneath the Franjo Tuđman Bridge. The Adriatic has a small tidal range, so berth depth rarely changes the plan, but the bura from the north-east and the jugo from the south-east can interrupt launch transfers and tender operations at the outer anchorage. Winter weather is more disruptive than summer, and it is in winter that most maintenance work is done.

Traffic splits sharply by season. From spring to autumn the harbour is dominated by cruise ships, some berthing at Gruž and others anchoring off the old town, and by the island ferries, which sail to Koločep, Lopud, Šipan and Mljet several times a day. A year-round ro-pax link runs to Bari in Italy, with its heaviest loading in summer. Cargo is smaller in scale than at Ploče or Rijeka and mostly serves the city and its hinterland: general cargo, project loads, bulk supplies and fuel arrive on coasters and short-sea ships that make brief calls.

For inspection, this mix produces two kinds of ship. Cruise vessels need scrubber and hull checks that fit around a day in port, with passengers ashore and the engine room under tight watchkeeping rules. Ferries and coasters need structural gauging that is planned months ahead, because the summer timetable leaves little room. Owners of older tonnage also use Gruž for condition checks before a charter, sale or docking elsewhere, and a record taken alongside in calm water gives the receiving yard and surveyor a measured picture to work from rather than an assumption.

facilities.h: Where ships can be gauged in and around Gruž
p: Most gauging in Dubrovnik is carried out afloat. Cruise ships on the Gruž berths can be worked on scrubber discharge lines, sea water cooling pipes and accessible tank boundaries during the call, once the master and chief engineer agree the spaces and the safety arrangements. Ferries on the Bari service and island lines stand at their own quays between sailings and overnight, and their vehicle decks and ramps are the usual first scope. The ship's agent, or the operator for ferries, arranges port passes, escort and any launch to the outer anchorage.

Heavy repair capacity in the immediate area is limited and aimed at small craft, so ships that need a full docking normally go to Split, Rijeka or a yard across the border in Montenegro. Gauging at Gruž before the ship sails lets the yard estimate steel from readings instead of guesses, and the same technicians can then travel on to the yard for the docking survey, keeping measurement points consistent. Lay-up of small ferries and workboats in winter, where it happens afloat, gives longer working windows than any call day.
list: Gruž cruise berths: scrubber overboard piping and technical spaces on cruise ships during the call, with passengers ashore
Island ferry quays at Gruž: vehicle deck, ramp and ballast tank gauging between Elafiti and Mljet sailings
Bari ro-pax berth: deck, stern door and tank gauging on the cross-Adriatic ferry between crossings
General cargo and fuel quays: hatch covers, holds and deck piping on coasters during or after cargo work
Outer anchorage off the old town: condition gauging by launch for charter, sale and off-hire checks in suitable weather
Winter lay-by berths in the inlet: longer-window gauging of ferries and workboats out of season

context.h: Port state control, EU rules and emissions context at Dubrovnik
p: Croatia is a Paris MoU member and part of the EU, so foreign ships in Dubrovnik are subject to the same port state control inspections as ships in Italian, Greek or French ports. Passenger ships in scheduled service, including the ro-pax ferries and the cruise ships that run regular itineraries, also fall under the additional EU inspection rules for passenger ro-ro craft. The national maritime administration sits in the Ministry of the Sea, Transport and Infrastructure, and Croatian-flag ferries are normally classed with the Croatian Register of Shipping, whose headquarters is a short coastal run north in Split.

EU measures shape owners' choices at Dubrovnik. Ships calling at EU ports have to carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation, which draws attention to older steel and coatings, and EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime set a carbon charge and an intensity target for voyages that start or end in the EU. For older ferries and coasters, those obligations sit next to steel condition when owners decide whether to docking-repair or retire a ship. Gauging results feed that decision directly, because a hull with measured margin can stay on the route and a hull with substantial corrosion cannot.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Dubrovnik
jobs.p: Dubrovnik work is set by the tourist season: tight call-day windows for cruise ships from spring to autumn, and longer refit and lay-up windows for ferries and workboats in winter. Owners and superintendents who plan the winter jobs early get the best choice of dates, and we agree scope, access and reporting format before the team leaves India, so that nothing is left to chase once the ship has sailed.
list: Scrubber wash-water and overboard piping gauging on a cruise ship during a call day at Gruž, timed around tender and passenger operations
Vehicle deck, ramp and ballast tank readings on an island car ferry in its winter lay-up, ahead of a docking at a yard along the Croatian coast
Stern door and ramp structure gauging on the Bari ro-pax between crossings, closing out items from the last annual survey
Hatch cover and hold gauging on a coaster at the cargo quay after discharge, supporting a sale to a new owner
Pre-docking steel estimate on a small passenger ship at a lay-by berth in the inlet, passed to the yard before the ship sails

logistics: Dubrovnik Airport at Ćilipi, south of the city, has European connections that thin out in winter, and Zagreb or Split offer alternatives with long road transfers. The ship's agent arranges ISPS passes for the Gruž quays and a launch for ships at the outer anchorage. Croatia is in the Schengen area, so the team from India travels on Schengen visas, and we ask for the sailing schedule early enough to allow for appointment lead times at the consulate.
vessels: Coasters and short-sea general cargo ships

faqs.q: Can you gauge a cruise ship's scrubber piping during a short call in Dubrovnik?
faqs.a: Often yes, if the spaces are accessible and the chief engineer agrees the scope in advance. Overboard piping, wash-water lines and valves near the shell can be gauged on a call day with the ship alongside at Gruž. Tank entry and hot work are handled under the ship's own permit system, and the team plans around watchkeeping and passenger operations.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock in Dubrovnik?
faqs.a: Not one suited to commercial ships of any size. Ships that need a docking normally go to Split, Rijeka or a yard across the border, and we gauge at Gruž first so the yard has steel estimates before the ship arrives. The same technicians can then attend the docking survey and keep the measurement locations unchanged.

faqs.q: When is the best time of year for ferry gauging at Gruž?
faqs.a: Winter lay-up, when island ferries and the Bari ro-pax are not on their full summer timetable. In season the work is limited to windows between sailings. Because refit periods are short and return-to-service dates fixed, bookings should be made months ahead, especially if tanks are to be opened for gauging.

faqs.q: Can a ship be gauged at the anchorage off the old town?
faqs.a: Yes, in suitable weather, by launch arranged through the agent. It is a practical route for owner's condition checks and pre-purchase work on small ships and yachts. Strong bura or jugo winds can suspend transfers, so we keep a weather margin in the schedule and confirm with the master on the day.
